summary: Replace the periodic-table staircase with a fixed group-by-stratum matrix whose cells visibly hold multiple elements. Encode stratum by row, reserve colour for hazards, expose law-participation counts, and present provisional entries as an explicitly labelled epistemic register.

tension_rulings.why: SPHERE, HELIX, and GRID assign visually salient positions without data meaning, inviting false relational readings.
The staircase makes vertical alignment look like shared stratum even though height is only a within-column ordinal.
Stratum and hazard cannot truthfully share nearby olive-to-red hues because viewers cannot reliably attribute the resulting colour.
A lanthanide-style pull-out conventionally signals space-saving displacement, not contested epistemic status.

findings.problem: The periodic-table metaphor implies that two coordinates uniquely locate an element, while up to seven elements occupy one group-stratum cell.
findings.instruction: Replace TABLE with a fixed 16-by-5 group-by-stratum matrix; make every intersection a bounded container holding a consistent small-multiple grid of its elements, with an explicit occupancy count.

findings.problem: Tiles at equal height can represent different strata, so the strongest positional cue directly contradicts the data.
findings.instruction: Remove minimum-stratum offsets and ordinal tile rows; give S0–S4 fixed, labelled rows and place every tile only within its actual stratum row.

findings.problem: The stratum heat ramp reaches rust while hazard semantics use iron-oxide red, making ordinary dependency depth visually indistinguishable from warning.
findings.instruction: Remove colour from stratum and encode it through fixed row position plus an explicit S0–S4 badge; reserve warning chroma for hazards and distinguish forbidden, elevated-hazard, and unverifiable with labelled glyphs or patterns.

findings.problem: The proposed encoding hides how many of the 29 required-bond laws name each element, making structurally frequent and rarely referenced mechanisms look equivalent.
findings.instruction: Add the raw law-participation count to each tile as a labelled integer or tick row and make it sortable; keep tile area constant and do not conflate this count with valence.

findings.section: Part 1 — Missing hazard denominator and Part 2 — Proposed visual direction
findings.problem: A hazard mark can be read as comparative risk or observed failure frequency even though the data contains failures without exposure or survivor counts.
findings.instruction: Encode only categorical hazard-rule membership and class, never hazard magnitude; place a persistent statement beside the legend that no exposure or survivor denominator exists.

findings.problem: The detached lanthanide-style strip makes provisional entries look displaced for geometric convenience instead of restricted because a criterion is contested.
findings.instruction: Use a separately framed and explicitly titled provisional register outside the matrix, state that its entries require a note, and avoid column alignment or styling that imitates a chemical-table pull-out.

what_to_keep: Keep the redundant non-colour status treatments so epistemic status remains legible independently of palette.
dissent_note: A visual-experience lens may value the inherited layouts as delight; this lens rejects them because meaningless position changes create false relational cues.
